newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn to issue 2-yr paper in auction next week - Buba.
newsitem.headline: Bonn to issue 2-yr paper in auction next week - Buba.

text.p: The German federal government will issue two-year Treasury Notes at an auction next week, the Bundesbank said on Monday.
The tender for the notes will be set on September 17, and bids are due by 0900 GMT on September 18, the Bundesbank said in a statement.
The Bundesbank did not state the volume of the issue and said details would be announced on September 17.
The volume will total up to 10 billion marks, according to the federal government's issue calendar for the third quarter of 1996.

Germany has pledged to issue two-year Treasury notes at quarterly auctions as part of a package of measures to aid the development of the domestic bond market by selling more short-term government debt.
Next week's auction will be the first such issue of two-year debt.

The government auctioned in July, for the first time, six-month Treasury Bills, or Bubills, in a sale that dealers said was a success. The Bubills, like the 2-year Treausry notes, will be issued quarterly.
